claim.summary: For every finite conjugation-closed configuration Z in the complete-grid Gram model with real even window phi supported in [-Lam/2,Lam/2]: ||G_Z||_HS^2 = ||phi||_2^-4 int_{-Lam}^{Lam} (phi^2*phi^2)(s) |S_Z(s)|^2 ds, S_Z(s) = sum_z m_z e^{-isz} = sum_real m e^{-is gamma} + 2 sum_j m_j e^{-is gamma_j} cosh(delta_j s).
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof from the bilinear Gram identity and conjugation invariance. Identifies the Hilbert-Schmidt norm at bandwidth Lam with a weighted mean square of the zero sum over |log x| <= Lam. Abstract statement about configurations; no estimate for zeta zeros.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Makes explicit that a second-moment premise at bandwidth Lam is a mean-square bound for the exponential sum over the points; expected to be the classical mean-square form of pair-correlation sums, novelty not claimed.
significance.next_action: Use for the cluster question: lower bounds for the mean square with positive integer coefficients.

mathematical_status.note: Complete proof in the entry; trapezoid-rule control against grid sums on 22 configurations agrees to the stated tolerance.

significance.note: Context-level identity; novelty not claimed and not searched in the literature.

relationships.note: Depends on the pair atom spectrum's bilinear Gram identity.

claim.summary: Flat window, complete grid, all points real, at most M_loc points (with multiplicity) per cell of length 2 pi/Lam over K consecutive cells: lambda_max(G_Z) <= M_loc (3 + (2/pi)(1 + ln K)); for every window ||G_Z||_HS^2 <= lambda_max(G_Z) * (number of points with multiplicity).
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof: Gram matrix of unit vectors, absolute row sums, the sinc decay. Shows that in the model a configuration of real points with a local count satisfies a second-moment bound at every bandwidth, so that bound is a consequence of the statement to be proved rather than an independent input.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Answers whether the second-moment premise beyond bandwidth log T follows from all points being real; it does, in the flat-window model, given a local count.
significance.next_action: None beyond use in the many-pair bound; a smooth-window version is not needed at present.

mathematical_status.note: Complete proof in the entry for the flat window; control on 18 configurations with real points tests the direction only.

relationships.note: Uses the trace statement of solitary amplification; used in the many-pair norm bound's reduction.

claim.summary: Complete-grid Gram model with n off-axis pairs, G = P + B: ||G||_HS >= ||B||_HS - ||P||_HS and lambda_max(G) >= ||B||_HS/(2n)^(3/2); ||B||_HS^2 >= 2 rho sum m_j^2 kappa_j^2 - sum m_j m_l (1 + kappa(delta_j - delta_l)) with rho the least eigenvalue of the normalized Gram matrix of the exponentials e^{-is z_j} in L^2(phi^2*phi^2); flat window with delta_j Lam >= 1, delta_j <= Delta and heights 8 Delta-separated: rho >= 3/5, and ||B||_HS >= kappa_max when kappa_max >= 5 M^2 + 1.
claim.assessment: Working proof. Extends solitary amplification to any number of off-line pairs with the loss stated exactly as rho; no loss in b for height-separated pairs. For clusters rho can be tiny and the bound empty, while sampled clusters show the true norm is not small, so the cluster case is open rather than obstructed. Conditional on an unavailable second-moment premise beyond bandwidth log T for any consequence about zeros.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Shows what a second-moment bound at large bandwidth would exclude (separated off-line pairs) and what it leaves (clusters); with the real configuration bound, shows the premise is close to a restatement of the goal for separated exceptions.
significance.next_action: Bound the mean square for clusters with positive integer multiplicities, or find a cluster of simple points with a loss beyond every power of b.

mathematical_status.note: Complete proof of all five parts in the entry; part 5 for the flat window only. Numerical control on 22 configurations.

significance.note: Context: delimits the Gram route in the model; not a result about zeta. Novelty not claimed.

relationships.note: Refines solitary amplification (n = 1 gives a solitary-type bound up to constants); depends on the pair atom spectrum, the second-moment identity's Gram interpretation and the real configuration bound; consistent with the two-pair cancellation.

claim.summary: For real even phi in L^2 supported in [-Lam/2,Lam/2], grid step 2pi/Lam over Z and v_z=(phihat(z-alpha_k))_k: v_z^T v_w = Lam (phi^2)^(z-w), v_z^* v_w = Lam (phi^2)^(w-conj z); a conjugate pair z, conj z off the real axis at distance delta has normalized atom (kappa+1) e_x e_x^T - (kappa-1) e_y e_y^T with kappa = int phi^2 cosh(2 delta u) / int phi^2 > 1.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof by Parseval on the interval and evenness. The bilinear identity is the imported density proof's Poisson identity; the Hermitian companion at complex arguments and the two-eigenvalue form are worked out here. Abstract complete-grid statement; says nothing about actual zeta zeros.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Elementary consequence of Fourier-series orthogonality, expected to be known in the explicit-formula literature; recorded as the model for the bridge test, no novelty claimed.
significance.next_action: Use for the many-pair cancellation computation; before applying to the imported cut form verify the tail hypothesis for its smoothed window.

mathematical_status.note: Complete proof in the entry for every bandwidth and every real even L^2 window supported in the interval; numerical control on four parameter pairs agrees.

significance.note: Context-level elementary lemma; novelty not claimed and not searched in the literature.

relationships.note: Extends the Poisson identity used in the imported density deduction to Hermitian products at complex arguments. Second moment of the complete-grid Gram form with several off-line pairs: new relationship with lem:gram-second-moment-identity, prop:many-pair-norm-bound.

claim.summary: In the complete-grid Gram form G_Z of a finite conjugation-closed configuration: trace = number of points with multiplicity regardless of position; at most p negative eigenvalues for p off-axis pairs; if exactly one pair is off the axis then ||G_Z||_HS >= lambda_max >= m(kappa+1), and >= (4/5) m (kappa+1) on a cut grid when kappa >= 2 and the pair vector's tail fraction is at most 1/16; kappa >= c (s'-s) e^{2 delta s} / ||phi||^2 when phi^2 >= c on s <= |u| <= s'.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof from the pair atom spectrum. At the imported bandwidth log T the resulting bound on a solitary off-line zero is delta <= 1/2 + o(1), which is vacuous; a restriction would need a second-moment bound at bandwidth theta log T with theta > 1, which is not available. The bound is not additive over pairs at constant cost (two-pair cancellation, a polylogarithmic loss); the many-pair case is unproved.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Identifies what the density proof's second moment does and does not say about one off-line zero; gives no restriction on zeta zeros from available premises.
significance.next_action: Determine the loss for n close off-axis pairs, and whether an adaptive test vector removes it.

mathematical_status.note: Complete proof of all six parts in the entry; the application to the imported cut form is not made because the tail hypothesis is unverified and the outcome at bandwidth log T is vacuous.

significance.note: Context: a precise statement of missing information for the route, not a result about zeta. Novelty not claimed.

relationships.note: Depends on the pair atom spectrum; limited by the two-pair cancellation. Second moment of the complete-grid Gram form with several off-line pairs: new relationship with lem:real-configuration-bound, prop:many-pair-norm-bound.

claim.summary: Flat window, complete grid, configuration {+-i delta, t +- i delta}: ||G_Z||_HS^2 = 4 + 4 kappa^2 + 4 sinc^2(t Lam/2) + 4 Re sinc^2((t+2i delta)Lam/2), kappa = sinh(b)/b, b = delta Lam; at t = pi/Lam and b >= pi/2 this is at most 4 + 16/pi^2 + 3 pi^2 kappa^2 / b^2, so no absolute c > 0 gives ||G_Z||_HS^2 >= c sum_j (kappa_j^2 + 1) over off-axis pairs.
claim.assessment: Refutation, by an exact identity, of the additive lower bound that would extend solitary amplification to several off-line pairs at constant cost. The loss shown is a factor of order b^-2 for two pairs; the loss for many close pairs is not computed.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Shows that a second-moment bound alone does not bound each off-line pair's contribution; the obstruction to passing from isolated zeros to all zeros in this model.
significance.next_action: Compute the n-pair loss and test adaptive test vectors.

mathematical_status.note: Exact sixteen-term computation with closed form at t = pi/Lam, proved in the entry and matched numerically at four parameter pairs with a no-cancellation control at t = 2 pi/Lam.

significance.note: Context: an explicit obstruction in the model. Novelty not claimed.

relationships.note: Refutes the many-pair extension of solitary amplification at constant cost; uses the pair atom spectrum's Gram identity for the flat window. Second moment of the complete-grid Gram form with several off-line pairs: new relationship with prop:many-pair-norm-bound.
